coachingPoints: The move is won by the shoulder, not the ball — sell the fake direction with your upper body.
Keep the bounce low: the ball should cross at shin height, never waist height.
One sharp move beats three lazy ones. A crossover should take less than one second.
Eyes up the whole time — watch the defender's chest and hips to read which way he bites.
Plant the outside foot and explode; the burst after the cross matters more than the cross itself.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the ball too wide and high across the body — fix: aim the cross at the inside of your opposite foot, low and tight.
Carrying the ball (palm under it) on the cross — fix: keep fingertips on top of the ball through the switch.
Faking only with the ball, not the body — fix: drop the shoulder and shift your weight toward the fake direction first.
Crossing back into the defender — fix: after the switch, take one hard dribble away from the defender, not toward him.
description: Switch the ball from one hand to the other in front of your body to beat a defender — the most famous move in basketball.
gameSituations: Beating a single defender in isolation — a sharp crossover freezes the on-ball defender and opens a driving lane.
Creating space for a pull-up — cross to move the defender, then stop and rise for the jumper before he recovers.
Attacking on the fast break — one crossover can be enough to get past the last defender between you and the basket.

howTo.detail: Dribble toward the defender on your right side with your body low. Let him think he has an angle on you — the trap is set by your posture.
howTo.title: Approach with the ball on one side

howTo.detail: Drop your shoulder, shift your weight, and glance toward the hand the ball is in. The defender must believe you are going that way.
howTo.title: Sell the fake with your shoulder

howTo.detail: In one quick motion, snap the ball low across your body to the other hand. The bounce should land just inside your opposite foot, below the knees.
howTo.title: Snap the ball low across your body

howTo.detail: At the same moment the ball crosses, plant your outside foot and push off hard. Your first step with the new hand must cover ground.
howTo.title: Explode out of the switch

howTo.detail: Take one or two hard, low dribbles away from the defender to finish separating. Never end the move dribbling in place.
howTo.title: Attack the space you created

title: Crossover Dribble
whatIsIt: The crossover is a ball-handling move where you bounce the ball from one hand to the other across the front of your body, usually low and fast. The purpose is simple: fake one direction, then explode the other way while the defender is leaning the wrong way.

It is the most recognizable move in basketball — and the most overused. A good crossover is not about style; it is about timing. One well-timed cross beats a defender; five flashy ones just give the defense time to recover.
whyItMatters: Almost every drive starts with a change of direction, and the crossover is the fastest way to do it. Players who own a reliable crossover can create their own shot anywhere on the floor, break down defenders in isolation, and collapse defenses that force help — which creates open looks for teammates.
